subject: Feature parity follow-up: tool-calls, structured outputs, streaming
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@epoch.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@epoch.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Feature parity follow-up: tool-calls, structured outputs, streaming

Hi Julia / Tom 1

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: validate Redwood for inference + tool/function calling, structured JSON outputs, and reliable streaming for Epoch's realtime agent.
- Biggest asks from Epoch: deterministic structured outputs, low tail latency for streaming, and an ability to function-call into internal services with secure payloads.

What we heard you want to test next:
1) End-to-end function-calling flow (tool discovery -> call -> structured output) with your sample tool schema.
2) Streaming response behavior (chunk sizes, latency, reconnection semantics) under realistic token rates.
3) Output fidelity and schema enforcement (JSON schema checks + evaluation harness).
4) Cost/latency comparison vs Hyperscaler A & B for your specific prompts.

Proposed next steps (can start this week):
- We attach a short feature-comparison matrix (redwood-vs-hyperscalers-matrix.xlsx) and a one-page test plan.
- Action: Redwood will spin up a temporary eval workspace and a streaming + function-calling harness. Dev will reach out about the technical details.
- Action: Epoch to share a representative prompt set, tool schemas, and an anonymized sample of expected traffic patterns (token lengths and concurrency).

Tentative schedule:
- Technical sync / test kickoff: Thu 2026-03-04 or Fri 2026-03-05 (we can be flexible).
- 3-day test window: Redwood runs parallel runs vs Hyperscaler endpoints and shares metrics.

I've attached the matrix for quick reference. Dev (cc'd) will follow up with exact endpoints and SDK examples.

Thanks 1
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa 1

A couple of clarifying Qs before we kick off: 

1) For function calling: can Redwood enforce required fields on the model side (so we can avoid post-hoc validation)? We observed inconsistent outputs from other providers.
2) For streaming: how do you handle partial JSON emission? Will the SDK reassemble reliably if the model emits JSON in chunks?
3) Data residency & logs: we need to confirm that logs from the eval workspace are isolated to the eval and won't be used for training / benchmarking beyond the test window.

I attached our internal requirements doc (epoch-requirements.pdf). It includes example tool schemas and a sample prompt set (redacted).

We can do the kickoff on Thu 2026-03-04 at 10:00 PT. Tom (cc) will bring our infra lead if available.

1Julia Park

julia@epoch.ai

Subject: Re: Feature parity follow-up: tool-calls, structured outputs, streaming

Perfect 1

Thu 10:00 PT works. Confirming actions before the call: 

- Epoch: please drop the prompt set + tool schemas into the Drive link I shared (or reply with attachments).
- Redwood (Dev): will provision an eval workspace with ephemeral keys and a test harness that runs:
   a) function-calling flow (we'll register your tool schema and run 100 calls across small/medium/large prompts)
   b) streaming test (sustained 100 tps at variable token rates up to 256 tokens / response)
   c) structured output checks (JSON schema enforcement + automatic scorecard)
- Deliverables after 3-day window: latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), tokens-per-second cost estimates, per-test output fidelity reports (examples + failure cases).

Quick notes on the questions from Julia: 
- Field enforcement: Redwood supports schema-guided decoding with a validation layer in the runtime; we can auto-reject outputs that don't parse (we'll log failures and show diffed examples). We won't silently mutate fields 1 failures will surface to the scorecard.
- Streaming + partial JSON: Our SDK exposes a reassembly utility that handles chunked JSON emission and will surface a parsing error event if reassembly fails; we also support resumable streaming with sequence tokens for idempotence.
- Eval workspace data: the temporary workspace will be isolated; logs are retained for the test window and are accessible only to your team and Redwood engineers on the test. Nothing from the eval is used to train Redwood models.

Attaching a short test plan (redwood-test-plan.md) and the matrix for context. Dev 1 please include a short curl + SDK example in your follow-up.

See you Thu at 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Feature parity follow-up: tool-calls, structured outputs, streaming

Hi all 1 quick technical follow-up and example snippets ahead of Thursday's kickoff. I'm Dev (SE on this engagement). Below are details for the test harness we'll provision and examples you can use immediately.

Eval workspace & credentials:
- We'll create an ephemeral project scoped to "epoch-eval-2026-03". You will get a short-lived API key (TTL 24h) for the kickoff tests; we can extend if needed. Keys are scoped to the project and do not cross-share.

Function-calling notes:
- Register your tool schema as a JSON Schema + type hints. Redwood will load the schema into the runtime and enable schema-guided decoding. If output doesn't parse to schema, we return a structured error with the "parse_fail" tag and include the raw model output for forensic analysis.

Streaming behavior & sample curl (chunk reassembly):
- Our streaming endpoint returns chunked events carrying: {event_type, seq, payload}. The client should append payloads in seq order and call the reassembly utility we provide. If a chunk is missed, you can request a re-stream from seq N.

Sample curl (streaming):
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <EPHEMERAL_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-std","prompt":"<your prompt>","stream":true,"max_tokens":256}'

Sample SDK (node) snippet 1 function calling + streaming reassembly (pseudo):
const r = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RDW_KEY });
const stream = await r.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-1-std', prompt, stream: true, function_schema });
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  reassembly.append(chunk);
  if (reassembly.complete()) {
    const parsed = reassembly.parseJson();
    // validate against schema, emit scorecard
  }
}

Latency testing and load:
- We'll run parallel clients to simulate the concurrency you provided (target: up to 50 concurrent requests, burst to 100 for 30s). We'll capture p50/p90/p99 and time-to-first-chunk for streaming.

Privacy / logs: logs for the ephemeral project will be viewable only by epoch-eval-2026-03 and Redwood SREs on-call for the tests; we do not retain artifacts beyond the agreed retention window (default 7 days for eval unless you request shorter).

If you want, I can post the exact curl + node snippets into the Drive folder so Tom's infra team can try locally before Thu.

1Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
